answer: Identities that misbehave lose their bond, so flooding the network with fake agents costs real capital per identity. A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is stake-weighted attestation: each agent locks a bond, and peers co-sign only work they verify. Like a comet burning up before it crosses the river, spam identities fail verification and forfeit stake, while legitimate agents on the tundra of low-reputation work still receive slowly through consistent peer attestation. Attackers must outspend every honest bond. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
